Working with his mother and brothers, he helped develop the business before the brothers separated their shipping interests. He retained Thenamaris, with operations spanning tankers, bulk carriers and gas transport, and his son Nikolas assumed its management.

long_biography.plain_text:
Greek shipowner Dinos Martinos financed the Benaki Museum's publication of the complete correspondence of poet Andreas Kalvos. The two volumes brought together letters written and received across the poet's life, with Greek translations of foreign-language originals. Detailed commentary, an index and a bibliography accompanied the texts.

With Lia Martinos, he founded KYKLOS, a centre for arts and cultures being developed in Piraeus. They commissioned Renzo Piano Building Workshop to design the institution. Its planned permanent collection focuses on art from Africa, Oceania and beyond, alongside temporary exhibitions, new commissions, performances and education programmes.
